On the spiral this is 2exp(t)[sinh(t)+kappa cos(alpha t)]. Positive crossings lie in negative-cosine lobes before L=asinh(kappa); each lobe center c_j<L yields two sign-change roots. On later lobes log(sinh(t)/(-cos(beta t))) has second derivative beta²sec²(beta t)-csch²(t)>0, hence ≤2 crossings per lobe. Fixed finitely many early lobes contribute O_beta(1) uniformly in kappa because their ratio has finitely many critical points. The center/lobe count gives N=beta L/pi+O_beta(1), not a mere lower bound. Alternating signs at j*pi/beta produce arbitrarily many distinct adversarial sites for affine non-phase-equivalent pairs. For the full trace distinct exponents j+k+i alpha(j-k) imply equality of all coefficient Gram entries, proving continuous uniqueness. Independent finite sign and root-count diagnostics agree but do not prove the universal quantifiers.
